static_traits.name: Zhang Ming
static_traits.family_status: Married with children, actively participating in children's sports activities
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with other parents involved in sports activities affected; has friends from the book club and parent-teacher association but not yet shared feelings
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychological counseling/treatment; no similar problems in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic; skeptical about counseling; marked self-denial; speech rate and other details not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I am always late every time I drive my children to sports competitions, which makes me believe I am useless.
basic_info.core_demands: When inferiority began affecting self-esteem and overall well-being, affecting my ability to enjoy daily activities, I decided to seek counseling, hoping to improve punctuality and relieve the feeling of 'being useless'.
growth_experiences: Two years ago the children started participating in more sports activities, requiring multiple pickups and dropoffs weekly while managing multiple schedules; initially the pressure was moderate, but as lateness became frequent, the belief of 'letting the children down' gradually reinforced, affecting relationships with other parents and increasing pressure and anxiety.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough, incompetent in the father role

special_situations.event: Arrives late when frequently shuttling children to sports activities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not punctual, it means I am a failure as a father/a useless person
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tightening schedule management, setting reminders, planning routes and times in advance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am late again, I am just useless, the children will be let down by me

special_situations.event: At the field or training site, sees other parents all able to arrange their children's activities punctually and calmly
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Must perform as well as other parents, otherwise it proves I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids communicating with other parents to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them, they must think I am incompetent

special_situations.event: Facing multiple schedules needing coordination at the same time (multiple children, multiple activities)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot handle all arrangements perfectly, I am completely no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to arrange all tasks perfectly in one go
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I simply cannot manage these arrangements, I am always late

special_situations.event: Even after investing much effort in planning, lateness still occurs
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If effort does not pay off immediately, it means I am essentially incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating their own progress and investment, further self-blame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Nothing I do is of any use

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be a competent, recognized good father
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as incompetent by other parents or children, fearing disappointing the children and being humiliated
defense_goal: Protecting self-esteem through avoiding socializing and self-reproach, reducing the risk of being evaluated

object_relations.object_representation: Critical others who look down on me (other parents)

object_relations.self_representation: A caregiver who disappoints the children
object_relations.object_representation: A child who needs my good care

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When interacting with other parents at my child's competitions or training venues, or when thinking about their views
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client subconsciously believes others will look down on them like judges (transference: projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use a supportive, non-judgmental tone; invite them to provide evidence and clarify specific facts, avoid labeling; gently question to guide them in distinguishing others' real feedback from their own speculation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes trying cognitive restructuring or behavioral experiments to change beliefs
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes change is ineffective, they are doomed to be 'no good' (transference: denial)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintain a steady, accepting tone; first empathize with their doubt, then suggest small-step trials; avoid forced persuasion, emphasize autonomous choice and pace.

manifestations: Feels daily life has changed from enjoyment to 'endurance', hard to gain satisfaction from activities
Decreased self-esteem drains life of vitality
Unwilling to share feelings with friends from the book club or parent-teacher association
Avoiding communication with other parents at the competition venue, feeling embarrassed and humiliated

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Withdrawing in social situations due to excessive worry about others' evaluations

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'
manifestations: Believing other parents 'look down on me', 'they must think I am incompetent'

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Avoiding communication with other parents, not seeking help from friends
Turns the need for outward expression into self-reproach and internal depletion

positive_force: Actively involved in the children's sports activities, willing to spend a lot of time picking up and dropping off
Willing to seek professional help (starting counseling)
Tries to organize the schedule and set reminders, with some time-management awareness
Having potential social support resources (friends from the book club, parent-teacher association)
negative_force: Comparing with others and mind reading, tending toward personalization, leading to avoiding socializing
Black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization, equating being late with 'complete failure'
Anxiety and increased stress, affecting enjoyment of and participation in daily activities

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance (avoiding communication with other parents at children's competitions or training)
antecedent: Seeing other parents at competitions/training sites
Thinking others may judge them as incompetent
target_behavior.core_reason: Mind reading and personalization cognitions cause shame and inferiority; avoidance reduces situational pressure
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal relationships damaged, reduced social support, worsening loneliness and inferiority

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecating speech and repeated self-blame (e.g. 'I am useless', 'I am not good enough'), accompanied by anxiety
antecedent: Lateness occurring or anticipating possible lateness
Trying to organize but still not fully punctual
target_behavior.core_reason: Black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, and the introjected rule of 'must be punctual'
target_behavior.function: Releasing the tension of guilt and anxiety in the short term, but maintaining the negative self-schema
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-esteem, persistent anxiety, further affecting time management and family interaction
